**Proof.**

Let $(B,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a regular local ring and $I\subset B$ an ideal with $B/I$ Gorenstein but not a complete intersection. We show $\operatorname{ht}(I)\notin\{0,1\}$.

Recall two standard facts we use throughout:

(F1) A regular local ring is Cohen–Macaulay (in fact a domain, even a UFD by Auslander–Buchsbaum).

(F2) If $B$ is regular local and $M$ is a finitely generated $B$-module of finite projective dimension that is Cohen–Macaulay, then by Auslander–Buchsbaum
$$\operatorname{pd}_B M=\operatorname{depth}B-\operatorname{depth}M=\dim B-\dim M=\operatorname{ht}(\operatorname{ann}M),$$
the last equality using that $B$ and $M$ are both CM. Moreover, for a CM module $M$ of finite pd, the **type** $r_B(M)$ equals the last Betti number $\beta_{\operatorname{pd}_B M}$ in the minimal $B$-free resolution of $M$ (obtained by dualizing the minimal resolution: $\operatorname{Ext}^p_B(M,B)\cong k^{\beta_p}$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_B(k,k^{\beta_p})\cong k^{\beta_p}$).

---

**Case $\operatorname{ht}(I)=0$.** Since $B$ is a regular local ring, it is a domain, so its only prime of height $0$ is $(0)$. The condition $\operatorname{ht}(I)=0$ means some prime minimal over $I$ has height $0$; the only possibility is $(0)$, hence $I\subseteq(0)$, i.e. $I=(0)$. Then $B/I=B$ is itself a regular local ring, hence a complete intersection (generated by the empty regular sequence). This contradicts the hypothesis that $B/I$ is not a complete intersection. So $\operatorname{ht}(I)\neq 0$.

---

**Case $\operatorname{ht}(I)=1$.** Since $B/I$ is Gorenstein, it is Cohen–Macaulay. Applying (F2) with $M=B/I$ (cyclic, so $\operatorname{ann}M=I$):
$$\operatorname{pd}_B(B/I)=\operatorname{ht}(I)=1.$$
The minimal $B$-free resolution of the cyclic module $B/I$ therefore has the form
$$0\longrightarrow B^{\beta_1}\xrightarrow{\;\varphi\;} B\longrightarrow B/I\longrightarrow 0,$$
where $\beta_1=\mu(I)$ is the minimal number of generators of $I$.

Because $B/I$ is Gorenstein, it is CM of **type $1$**. By (F2), the type equals the last Betti number:
$$1=r_B(B/I)=\beta_1.$$
Hence $\mu(I)=1$, i.e. $I=(f)$ is principal. Since $B$ is a domain and $I\neq(0)$ (as $\operatorname{ht}(I)=1>0$), the element $f$ is a non-zerodivisor; thus $f$ is a regular sequence of length $1$. By definition $B/I=B/(f)$ is then a **complete intersection**.

This again contradicts the hypothesis that $B/I$ is not a complete intersection. So $\operatorname{ht}(I)\neq 1$.

---

Combining both cases, $\operatorname{ht}(I)$ can be neither $0$ nor $1$. $\blacksquare$
